position: Other Offices and Bureaus (Bureau for Foreign Assistance; Office of Budget Resources and Management; Bureau for Legislative and Public Affairs)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the State Department's foreign assistance office (F), led by the USAID Administrator at Deputy Secretary rank, refocus most staff from preparing the annual budget proposal to executing appropriated money. It calls for dropping the duplicative Mission and Bureau Resource Requests, delivering the section 653(a) Foreign Assistance Act report to Congress within 60 days, fast-tracking congressional notifications and other pre-obligation steps, and publishing all notifications and reports.
remaining: A published State process that eliminates duplicative budget request cycles in favor of execution.
Delivery of the section 653(a) allocation report within 60 days of appropriation, shown by dated transmittals.
A documented fast-track for congressional notifications.
Public posting of all notifications and reports as a general practice.

status_summary: No source found shows the Mandate's process changes for the foreign assistance office: no end to the Mission and Bureau Resource Requests, no 60-day section 653(a) report, no fast-track for congressional notifications and no policy of publishing all notifications and reports. In the successor structure USAID no longer exists (its remaining operations merged into State on 2025-07-01), and State Delegation of Authority No. 597 (published 2025-09-05) placed the Director of Foreign Assistance's powers under an Under Secretary, while the FY2026 explanatory statement makes enacted amounts available regardless of when the 653(a) report is sent. GAO reported on 2026-09-30 that State paused all new obligations on 2025-01-24 pending review, and a special message of 2025-08-28 proposed rescinding nearly 5 billion dollars of foreign aid funds shortly before they expired, which the Supreme Court let stand on an interim basis on 2025-09-26. These steps slowed rather than sped the availability of funds, but they concern whether funds are spent rather than the budget and notification process the text addresses, so the record stays at not_started rather than diverged.

timeline.event: NPR reported that one official served as USAID Deputy Administrator and State Director of Foreign Assistance and that his signature appeared on orders cancelling about 5,200 programs.
USAID's remaining operations were merged into the State Department, ending the agency that the Mandate would have placed in charge of the F office.

A special message proposed rescinding nearly 5 billion dollars of foreign assistance funds; according to CRS (Legal Sidebar of 2025-09-25), OMB then reapportioned the funds so they were unavailable for obligation, with fewer than 45 days left before they expired.

State published Delegation of Authority No. 597, placing the Director of Foreign Assistance's powers and those of five other aid-related offices under an Under Secretary for Foreign Assistance, Humanitarian Affairs, and Religious Freedom.

The Supreme Court granted a stay, pending appeal, of a district court order requiring obligation of expiring foreign aid funds, as to the funds covered by the 2025-08-28 special message; the order states it is not a final ruling on the merits.
